title: Mechanism of life-long maintenance of neuron identity despite molecular fluctuations.
authors: Traets, Joleen Jh; van der Burght, Servaas N; Rademakers, Suzanne; Jansen, Gert; van Zon, Jeroen S
one_liner_zh: 该文通过模拟与实验研究转录因子CHE-1结合自身启动子维持神经元命运的机制，涉及TF-DNA结合与动态调控，但以生物学机制为主，AI/物理模拟方法深度有限。
abstract: Cell fate is maintained over long timescales, yet molecular fluctuations can lead to spontaneous loss of this differentiated state. Our simulations identified a possible mechanism that explains life-long maintenance of ASE neuron fate in Caenorhabditis elegans by the terminal selector transcription factor CHE-1. Here, fluctuations in CHE-1 level are buffered by the reservoir of CHE-1 bound at its target promoters, which ensures continued che-1 expression by preferentially binding the che-1 promoter. We provide experimental evidence for this mechanism by showing that che-1 expression was resilient to induced transient CHE-1 depletion, while both expression of CHE-1 targets and ASE function were lost. We identified a 130 bp che-1 promoter fragment responsible for this resilience, with deletion of a homeodomain binding site in this fragment causing stochastic loss of ASE identity long after its determination. Because network architectures that support this mechanism are highly conserved in cell differentiation, it may explain stable cell fate maintenance in many systems.
abstract_zh: 细胞命运在长时间尺度上得以维持，然而分子波动可能导致这种分化状态的自发丧失。我们的模拟识别出一种可能机制，解释了线虫（Caenorhabditis elegans）中末端选择器转录因子CHE-1如何维持ASE神经元命运的终身稳定性。在此机制中，CHE-1水平的波动被其结合在目标启动子上的CHE-1储备所缓冲，该储备通过优先结合che-1启动子确保持续的che-1表达。我们通过实验证据支持这一机制，表明che-1表达对诱导的瞬时CHE-1耗竭具有韧性，而CHE-1靶标的表达及ASE功能则丧失。我们鉴定出一个130 bp的che-1启动子片段负责这种韧性，该片段中同源域结合位点的缺失导致ASE身份在其确定后长时间随机丧失。由于支持此机制的调控网络架构在细胞分化中高度保守，这可能解释了许多系统中稳定细胞命运的维持。
